# Vendored Packages

This directory contains source-vendored copies of the Cordis framework and its foundation libraries. They are copied into this monorepo instead of being depended on via npm, so that the harness fully owns its framework layer (auditable, patchable, pinned).

All vendored packages are **renamed into the `@qilin-agent` scope** (`cordis` → `@qilin-agent/kylin`, `@cordisjs/plugin-<x>` → `@qilin-agent/kylin-plugin-<x>`): every harness package declares `@qilin-agent/kylin` as a peer dependency, so publishing the harness publishes this framework layer too, and a publication under the upstream names would squat them on the registry. Directory names and upstream version numbers are deliberately unchanged, so the manifest below still reads as an upstream snapshot. `pnpm-workspace.yaml#linkWorkspacePackages` makes those preserved semver ranges resolve these pinned workspaces, including imports from built `lib/`. The `hygiene` gate `verify-vendored-links` asserts every vendored name resolves to a workspace `link:` in `pnpm-lock.yaml` with no registry copy alongside. Schemastery's manifest additionally declares a conditional `exports` map (import → `.mjs`, require → `.cjs`): pnpm links the directory itself, so without `exports` Node's ESM resolver would fall back to `main` and load the CJS entry whose lazy `require('@qilin-agent/cosmokit')` can race ESM loading of the same linked module under module-hook hosts (vitest). Upstream MIT `LICENSE` files are preserved in each package directory.

This file covers the manifest, the local-modification log, and the procedure for **updating** an existing vendored package. To **add a new** one, see the cookbook guide: [docs/cookbook/adding-a-vendored-package.md](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-vendored-package.md).

The [Cordis rc.11 upgrade plan](cordis-rc11-upgrade-plan.md) records the package scope, PR dependencies and disposition of the local modifications; every step in it has landed in this tree. Upstream release labels decouple from vendored source content (a release can bump vendor version fields without moving `vendor/*/src`), so capability judgements read the manifest and sources, never the version number alone.

Group, HMR and Logger-console stay on their previous commit: upstream did not move them either, and the only upstream HMR change is the three-line `Include.refresh()` capture in V9. HMR `1.1.1` has no upstream source yet (the upstream manifest still pins `1.0.15`), so its source upgrade is not part of this tree.

Third-party dependencies of the vendored packages stay on npm: `@standard-schema/spec`, `js-yaml`, `chokidar`, `picomatch`, `@babel/code-frame`, `supports-color`, `node-addon-require-builtin`.

Intentionally **not** vendored (verified unused by this set): `reggol`, `@cordisjs/utils`, `@cordisjs/element`, `@cordisjs/unyaml` (dev-time YAML import hook only).

## Local modifications

Keep this log exhaustive — every divergence from upstream must be listed. Each entry has a stable ID: remove an entry when its divergence no longer exists, and never renumber or reuse IDs. The next new entry is V28. The IDs match the upstream log of the same tag, so an entry can be compared without translating numbers: upstream retired V8, V12, V13, V18, V19, V20 and V21 and added V25–V27 in the same release.

After the rc.11 sync the vendored sources equal the upstream tag's `vendor/` tree file for file; the remaining divergences are the manifest metadata (repository URL, engines, versions) and the entries below.

- **V1 · `hmr/src/index.ts`**: removed the `./locales/en-US.yml` / `./locales/zh-CN.yml` imports, the `.i18n({...})` call on the `Config` schema, and the `src/locales/` directory. Rationale: those imports require a runtime YAML loader hook (`@cordisjs/unyaml`) that we do not vendor; the i18n texts only localize config descriptions.
- **V2 · All `package.json` files**: regenerated for QiLin releases with `@qilin-agent` names, versions taken from the upstream tag's manifest, precise bundled-runtime and `lib/types/**/*.d.ts` / `.d.ts.map` file entries, source exports where applicable, and declaration metadata pointing at `lib/types`. Dependency and peer-dependency ranges are preserved except that `hmr` declares `esbuild` as a direct dev dependency because its source imports the `BuildFailure` type and pnpm's strict workspace resolution requires the owner package to name that dependency, and `loader` requires `node-addon-require-builtin` to match the runtime used by published app packages. The `repository` URL points at this repository and `engines` carries QiLin's Node range, so these files are the one vendored surface that is not an upstream snapshot.
- **V3 · All `tsconfig.json` files**: regenerated to extend the repo-root `tsconfig.base.json`, emit TypeScript intermediates to `lib/types`, and declare project references.
- **V4 · Vendored TypeScript source internal specifiers**: changed local relative imports/exports from upstream's specifier shape to explicit `.ts` specifiers so TypeScript rewrites emitted JS to `.js` while declarations keep explicit, NodeNext-safe `.ts` specifiers. This includes `loader/src/config/isolate.ts` using `declare module './entry.ts'`. Type-only dependencies use `import type` or inline `type` modifiers so ESM output does not retain erased interfaces.
- **V5 · `schemastery/tsdown.config.ts` and `logger-console/tsdown.config.ts`**: ours, not upstream files — per-package build-shape overrides (dual ESM+CJS output; separate node/browser entries) for the repo-root tsdown build. They read the JS emitted under `lib/types` and then write the publish runtime entries under `lib/`. Like the regenerated tsconfigs, they are not part of the upstream sync surface.
- **V6 · `cordis/src/fiber.ts` lifecycle hardening**: the reentrant disposal guarantees rc.11 owns — an effect's owner-list wrapper registered before its setup body, cleanup retained until quiescence, effect creation rejected while the owner is `UNLOADING`, child fibers published only after their parent-owned disposer exists, per-observer containment of teardown failures, and superseded activations that cannot fail the replacement state. Upstream retired the surrounding local wrapper in this release; the vendored file is upstream's, not a QiLin patch.
- **V7 · Cordis, Loader and Timer JSDoc enrichment**: `@param`/`@returns` tags and contract documentation (disposal semantics, waterfall veto, bail conditions, error cases) across the public plugin-author surface — `Context` (class, statics, and the `Context` interface properties incl. `root`), module re-exports, shared utility helpers, `EventsService`, `Fiber`, `RegistryService`, `ReflectService`, `Service`, `LoggerService` and their `declare module './context.ts'` overloads. The upstream `EventsService.dispatch()` deprecation annotation is omitted: QiLin enumerates callbacks to contain each observer failure independently, which the typed dispatch methods do not provide. Timer retains its local class and helper summaries; its README is local documentation because the upstream package has none. Comment-only; no code changes. Motivation: the website API-reference generator renders these docs and hard-errors on undocumented members. Retire this entry when the enrichment is upstreamed.
- **V9 · `hmr/src/index.ts` module-watcher readiness and native paths**: realpath the existing watch base, classify framework modules and attach listeners before reporting readiness, and compare config paths using both canonical and configured spellings. This preserves Node module-cache identity across Windows short-name paths and filesystem aliases. The main watcher uses `ignoreInitial: true` so startup reads do not trigger another refresh; exact profile patch watching is owned by `packages/boot/hmr/src/watch-config.ts`. The Include change listener logs a rejected `Include.refresh()` instead of leaving the rejection unhandled; the rejection reports unsaved runtime changes while Include keeps its running tree. Covered by `packages/boot/hmr/tests/watch-config.spec.ts` and `scripts/kylin-vendor-hmr-include.spec.ts`.
- **V10 · Vendored Node-compatible TypeScript**: marked erased imports explicitly across `cordis`, `loader`, `include`, `hmr`, and `schemastery` so Node's native TypeScript transform does not request types as runtime exports. Schemastery's source uses an ESM default export and its package declares `type: module`. Conditional exports select `.mjs` for import and `.cjs` for require; without them, concurrent imports under module-hook hosts reach the CJS entry and can race its require of ESM Cosmokit (`ERR_REQUIRE_ESM_RACE_CONDITION`).
- **V11 · Include patch and YAML exports**: `include/src/index.ts` exports upstream `applyPatches` as `applyEntryPatches` and the `!!js` YAML dialect as `entryListSchema`, so `qilin --dump-config` composes entries with the same algorithm that mounting uses. The returned list is always a `structuredClone`, so callers must not rely on object identity; the upstream patch index already addresses rows inserted earlier in the same patch list. Covered by `packages/boot/app-boot/tests/config-reload.spec.ts` and `scripts/kylin-entry-commit.spec.ts`.
- **V14 · Include persistence results**: `include/src/index.ts` keeps an error for unsaved journal changes. `flush()` retries pending writes and rejects while changes remain unsaved; `stop()` returns the same result and always stops the child tree; a later successful flush clears previous errors. A failed `refresh()` can also reject while runtime changes remain unsaved. Patch-owned changes route to the parent Include, so callers that need them persisted must flush that parent too. The constructor omits upstream's `ctx.hmr.watch(this.filename, () => this.refresh())` registration because neither HMR provider exposes `watch()`; both find each Include by scanning loader entries for its `filename` and call `refresh()`. Ordinary Fiber teardown keeps its error containment. Covered by `scripts/kylin-include-journal.spec.ts` and `packages/host/directory-picker-auto/tests/loader-composition.spec.ts`.
- **V15 · Configuration access across Core, Loader, Include and HMR**: rc.11 Core owns raw `Fiber.config`, `internal/config(fiber, next)`, `internal/commit` and awaited `internal/update(config, next)`. Root-fiber candidate resolution remains available without a plugin schema. Local `rawConfig`, `resolveConfig(candidate)` and `effectiveConfig` accessors retain the DSH consumer API. Fiber caches the object passed to activation or a successful update that keeps the instance; candidate resolution is pure, failed or superseded updates cannot replace the cache, and volatile updates retain references. Loader resolves only entry roots and excludes Group/Include tree carriers, so nested `!!js` expressions wait for their own injections. Include retains its tree-carrier marker and public patch exports, and HMR transfers raw config through the accessors. Consumers that display or persist configuration read `effectiveConfig`; `config` is raw input and may still hold `!!js` nodes. Covered by `scripts/kylin-config-access.spec.ts`, `scripts/kylin-core-lifecycle.spec.ts` and the boot/HMR suites.
- **V16 · `cordis/package.json` publishes `src`**: added `src` to the `files` list, joining the other eight vendored packages. Cordis declares `"./src/*": "./src/*"` in its exports, so a tarball without `src` publishes an export map pointing at absent files; the release change judgement also reads `files` to decide whether a diff reaches the payload, and a package whose only published paths are build output has no tracked path to match.
17. **`@qilin-agent` rescope**: every vendored manifest `name`, every internal dependency entry among the vendored set, and every module specifier that reaches them use the scoped names in the manifest table's `npm name` column. Directory names, version numbers, and dependency ranges are unchanged, and no upstream runtime identifier is renamed — `Symbol.for('schemastery')` and Schemastery's `vendor:` metadata field keep their upstream values. Re-apply with `pnpm run rescope-vendor --apply` after a sync; the table's two name columns are the mapping, restated for consumers in [docs/rescope.md](../docs/rescope.md).
- **V22 · Volatile config across `cosmokit`, `schemastery`, `cordis`, and `loader`**: Cosmokit supplies immutable references and framework-owned commits; `deepEqual` treats two references as equal, propagates strict comparison into arrays, compares every array slot with holes treated as undefined, handles cycles conservatively, compares URLs by normalized href, and compares other opaque objects by identity in strict mode. Schemastery adds `.volatile()`, optional/default inference, placement validation without eager lazy-schema expansion, metadata-free serialized node compatibility, serialized metadata, reference-aware simplification, unsupported volatile values reported as `ValidationError` with their path, and `.default()` accepting the raw input type `Partial<S>`. Loader's save path calls `simplify` with its schema receiver (`unparse.call`). Loader compares raw options strictly in `Entry.update`; for a config-only change on an active fiber it calls the pure `equalExceptVolatile` function in `config/diff.ts`, which narrows the Standard Schema to Schemastery's `Schema` type and recursively skips fixed volatile paths using schema metadata without executing config hooks or validation. Missing or null object nodes compare using their declared defaults, including nodes without volatile descendants; schema backedges retain raw comparison. For a volatile-only change, `Entry._commitVolatile` takes the canonical fiber `entry.fiber.ctx.fiber`, re-parses the raw config through `Fiber.resolveConfig()`, compares ordinary effective values, commits references and emits the instance-local `loader/volatile-update`. A changed ordinary effective value falls back to the ordinary remount, and an invalid candidate is logged while the raw config stays retained for the next activation. Code replacement tests live in `packages/boot/hmr/tests/modules.spec.ts`; schema and Loader tests in `scripts/volatile-config.spec.ts` and `scripts/loader-volatile-update.spec.ts`.
- **V23 · `loader/src/config/entry.ts` module identity**: retains each entry's raw import result as `moduleNamespace`, before plugin export normalization. HMR matches that object to Node's cached module namespace and updates it after a successful reload. `EntryTree.import()` keeps its existing arguments and return value; `loader/README.md` documents the additive field. Covered by `packages/boot/hmr/tests/modules.spec.ts`.
- **V24 · `timer/locale/{en,zh}.json` display metadata**: local English and Chinese titles and descriptions for the Settings plugin inventory; `timer/package.json` exports and publishes these locale resources.
- **V25 · Loader lifecycle adaptations**: before a combined context/config update, Loader refreshes dependencies locally (`fiber._checkImpl` for every injection), which prevents activation against stale isolation bindings; disabled-entry updates await disposal. `loader/patch-context` is a waterfall whose listeners may be async, so an entry update awaits the restart it triggers. A failed fiber requires an explicit `update()` to recover, including after its dependencies change.
- **V26 · `loader/src/config/tree.ts` cross-tree moves**: backports [cordiverse/cordis#271](https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis/pull/271), merged after `v4.0.0-rc.11`. When `EntryTree.update()` moves an entry into a group of another tree, the entry and the same-tree members of its group move their store registrations to the target tree, and the move is rejected before either tree changes when the target tree already holds one of their ids. The source tree receives a removal and the target tree a creation, without `legacy` or `from`. Retire this entry when the vendored Loader includes the upstream fix. Covered by `scripts/kylin-include-journal.spec.ts`.
- **V27 · `loader/src/config/tree.ts` explicit ids with `:`**: `ensureId()` accepts explicit ids containing `EntryTree.sep`; upstream rejects them. Generated bundles prefix their row ids with `<package name>:`, and installed profiles already contain such rows. `resolve()` still splits ids on `:`, so these entries cannot be addressed by nested path. Rows installed from bundles authored upstream already carry such ids, so a strict separator check would reject them. Covered by `scripts/kylin-entry-commit.spec.ts`.

### Retired entries

Each of these was a QiLin-local entry before the rc.11 sync. The ID is retired and never reused; the behaviour below is either upstream's now or was never present in the source.

- **V8 · transactional Loader/Include reconciliation — never present in source.** The entry claimed that Loader imports a changed entry before disposal and restores the previous plugin on failure, and that Include applies patches to a clone before committing. A search for `rollback`/`restore`/`previous` state in `loader/src/{index,config/entry,config/tree}.ts` and `include/src/index.ts` found no such mechanism. The guarantees that do exist come from upstream: `EntryGroup.update` attempts every listed row and reports failures, Include validates detached candidate content before committing its cache, and a failed fiber stays failed until an explicit update (V25).
- **V12 · Include serialization plus HMR `ignoreInitial` — superseded.** The entry claimed every child-tree mutation ran through one queue; the old source had only a debounced `writeTask` and no `_applyTask`/`_loop`. The journal's `_applyTask`/`_loop`/`_drain` own serialization now (V14), and the HMR `ignoreInitial` half is part of V9.
- **V13 · `writeTask` type widening**: the field no longer exists; Include's journal owns pending writes.
- **V18 · `disabled` expression interpolation**: upstream's `Entry._resolveDisabled` owns the `!!js` evaluation, so only the behavioural tests remain QiLin's.
- **V19 · Loader runtime shape detection**: upstream's `ModuleLoader.fromInternal()` classifies the loader by the module-job API it owns (`getOrCreateModuleJob` for the v2 loader, `getModuleJobForImport` for v1) instead of by Node major version, matching what this tree needed.
- **V20 · Entry fiber identity**: `Entry._init` stores the registry wrapper, and every identity comparison goes through `fiber.ctx.fiber` (V15). Consumers that compared `entry.fiber === fiber` were updated with the sync.
- **V21 · Logger exporter disposer**: `LoggerService.exporter()` already retains its registration id in the vendored source of both releases; no divergence remains.

### Resolver adaptations

Relative to the resolver source in Cordis `v4.0.0-rc.11`:

- **Web build imports:** `loader/src/resolve.ts` uses default imports for Node builtin modules to support the Web shell's browser externalization. The shell supplies its own module loader.
- **Package-scope cache keys:** `loader/src/resolve.ts` normalizes directory paths with `path.resolve()` before finding the package scope. A root config and a nested config in the same package therefore share the same cached resolver promise and helper-file write. Covered by `scripts/kylin-loader-resolve.spec.ts`.

## Sync procedure

To update a vendored package from upstream:

1. In the upstream workspace, note `git rev-parse HEAD` of the relevant submodule.
2. Copy the package's `src/` (and `bin.js`, `README.md`, `LICENSE` if changed) over the vendored directory.
3. Re-apply the local modifications listed above (or drop them if upstream made them unnecessary — update the log either way, retiring the ID).
4. Update the version and commit hash in the manifest table.
5. Run `pnpm install && pnpm run test && pnpm run build` at the repo root.
